transcript: Tonight, I was at MCC attending The Connector, a new Jason Robert Brown musical. It stars Hannah Cruz and Ben Levi Ross as two journalists in the 90s in New York. I knew of Ben Levi Ross because he's played Evan Hansen, a character not very dissimilar from the character he plays here. The score being by Jason Robert Brown is 100% what compelled me to buy a ticket, and although it wasn't my favorite score by him, I mean the standard is so high and this score definitely didn't disappoint. The way his music is so conversationally melodic is on full display here and the singing was fantastic. The premise wasn't the most interesting to me but it definitely got more engaging as it progressed and as I reflect on the plot in retrospect, I’m left with a lot of questions. On one hand, this is kind of frustrating but on another, it makes sense given the themes of the show. Another thing I was kind of conflicted about was the production design, which is mostly pretty stark so, on brand with the show but you know I kind of wish it had been a little more aesthetically pleasing. And same with the choreography which was very formation driven and angular so at times this was cool but other times I thought it looked a bit clunky. In the end, I thought it was a cool piece but it's not screaming Broadway to me just yet. With that, another program for my collection.
